title: 'I Quit' Match Confirmed For AEW Double Or Nothing 2026, Swerve Strickland's AEW Return - NewsBreak
text:
By Ryan Clark ,
1 hours ago
This week’s episode of AEW Dynamite opened with a high-stakes title match, as Kevin Knight put his TNT Championship on the line against MJF. The bout came together after the two traded heated words during a tense promo segment on the April 22 episode.
In the closing moments, MJF tried to tilt the odds in his favor by bringing the TNT Championship into the ring, but referee Bryce Remsburg quickly confiscated it. With the official distracted, Friedman reached for his diamond ring, only for Knight to beat him to the punch with a low blow. Capitalizing instantly, “The Jet” rolled MJF up in a tight small package to secure the win.
After the match, Darby Allin descended from above and backed up Knight, chasing MJF off. Allin then offered Knight an opportunity at the AEW World Championship on next week’s Dynamite.
Christian Cage and Adam Copeland have officially raised the stakes for AEW Double Or Nothing 2026.

During the April 25 episode of AEW Collision, Dax Harwood and Cash Wheeler accepted the challenge from Copeland and Cage — but only if the match is contested under “I Quit” rules.
Just days later on Dynamite, Copeland and Cage made it clear that they were on board, confirming the added stipulation during an interview with Renee Paquette.
Swerve Strickland appears to be closing in on his AEW return — and he may already have his next target lined up.
During Wednesday’s episode of AEW Dynamite, a cinematic vignette aired set in a dusty Western town. The scene unfolded with chaos erupting inside a saloon as frightened patrons scrambled to get out. Moments later, a bloodied man was thrown through the doors and stumbled away, clearing the path for a mysterious figure to emerge.
That figure was revealed to be Strickland, accompanied by Prince Nana. As the two made their way forward, Strickland spotted a “Wanted” poster for Bandido lying on the ground. He picked it up, studied it briefly, and then set it ablaze — sending a clear message about his intentions.
Strickland has been absent from AEW programming since his loss to Kenny Omega on the March 25 episode of Dynamite, where he came up short in a high-stakes match for a future AEW World Championship opportunity. Omega also put his executive vice president status on the line in that bout.
There’s still no official word on when Strickland will return to in-ring action or if a showdown with Bandido is imminent. Bandido, meanwhile, continues to reign as ROH World Champion and has held the title for 389 days.
